What should a good trade website include?

The essentials that help visitors understand your work, trust your business and get in touch.

By TradeBuilt · 25 September 2026

A good trade website helps a potential customer make a decision. It explains what you do, where you work and how to contact you, without making them hunt for the answer.

Start with your services and areas

A visitor should quickly understand whether you can help with their job. Be specific about your services and the areas you cover. A roofing company, for example, might explain roof repairs, replacements and flat roofing separately.

Use familiar terms your customers recognise. Describe what the service involves and the situations it is suitable for. A short, clear explanation is more useful than a long list of broad claims.

Show evidence of your work

Use photographs of real projects when you have permission to publish them. Explain the work completed, the problem solved and any details that show your care and experience.

Only include qualifications, accreditations and customer feedback you can substantiate. Specific evidence gives people something concrete to assess.

Make contact straightforward

Give visitors an obvious way to call or send an enquiry. Keep forms focused on the information you need to respond, and explain what will happen after submission.

Check the experience on your own phone. Can you read the text comfortably? Are buttons easy to tap? Is your phone number easy to find?

Keep the basics current

Review your contact details, services and coverage as your business changes. Remove services you no longer offer and avoid leaving outdated information where a customer could rely on it.

A website does not need to say everything. It needs to answer the important questions and make the next step clear.
